_doc: Revert-verify mutants for vault-exodev ems__Bug 2653916f: the aggregation step of SPARQL 1.1 (§18.2.4.1 grouping, §18.2.4.2 HAVING) — GROUP BY over an empty input has no group, HAVING without grouping is a Filter, an aggregate in ORDER BY groups the level, EXISTS works in HAVING and SELECT expressions. Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect` (pairwise distinct across the four specs of this harness). `red_re` anchors on the jest failure header `● <suite> › <axis> ` (ITRV §A44/§A104). C1–C3 are controls; A12 and A18 lock unchanged behaviour and are green on the pre-fix engine by construction. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders — run the matrix on a copy with the paths substituted (§A145).

M3_select_no_explicit_flag._note: SELECT does not mark GROUP BY on the node: GROUP BY by an expression over an empty input answers the phantom row again (A2); ASK still right ⇒ the differential reddens.
M3_select_no_explicit_flag.from:
...(explicitGroup ? { explicit: true } : {}),
        variables: groupVars,
        aggregates,
        having: havingExpressions.length > 0 ? havingExpressions : undefined,
        input: operation,
M3_select_no_explicit_flag.to:
...(explicitGroup ? { explicit: false } : {}),
        variables: groupVars,
        aggregates,
        having: havingExpressions.length > 0 ? havingExpressions : undefined,
        input: operation,

M4_ask_no_explicit_flag._note: The same for ASK (A2b) — the two group blocks are separate code, each needs its axis.
M4_ask_no_explicit_flag.from:
...(explicitGroup ? { explicit: true } : {}),
        variables: groupVars,
        aggregates,
        having: havingExpressions.length > 0 ? havingExpressions : undefined,
        input: where,
M4_ask_no_explicit_flag.to:
...(explicitGroup ? { explicit: false } : {}),
        variables: groupVars,
        aggregates,
        having: havingExpressions.length > 0 ? havingExpressions : undefined,
        input: where,

M5_select_having_builds_group._note: The pre-fix condition in SELECT: HAVING alone builds a group, so HAVING without an aggregate collapses the solutions into one empty row (form 2). Spec stage: also A25 — a group built for HAVING answers one empty row where the FILTER twin keeps the solutions.

M6_ask_having_builds_group._note: The pre-fix condition in ASK only: ASK answers by the old group, SELECT by the Filter. Spec stage: also A23 / A24 (an ASK group has no ?l, so HAVING (?l = …) and IN are false) and A25 (ASK HAVING differs from its FILTER twin).

M7_having_filter_first_only._note: Plausible wrong Filter: only the first HAVING condition is kept (A6).

M8_having_filter_via_aggregate_table._note: The Filter is translated through the aggregate-aware operator table instead of the full expression translator: IN in HAVING without grouping drops its list (A4). Spec stage: also A24 — the aggregate-aware table loses the IN list on the ASK path too.

M9_order_aggregates_not_collected._note: ORDER BY aggregates are not collected (SELECT and ASK): SELECT refuses the query again, ASK builds no group (form 3).

M10_order_comparator_without_map._note: The comparator of an aggregate condition is translated without the aggregate map: the group exists, but SELECT refuses the ORDER BY condition; ASK unaffected.

M11_ask_order_not_collected._note: ASK ignores the aggregate in ORDER BY again (pre-fix ASK): no implicit group.

M18_select_group_ignores_order_aggregate._note: Review X2: the ORDER BY aggregates are collected, but SELECT decides whether to group from the count taken before them — the most natural form of it is ORDER BY left where it was. Only a level whose ONLY aggregate is in ORDER BY tells (A9b).

M19_counter_reset_per_level._note: Review R4: the aggregate-name counter is reset in translateSelect again. A subquery inside EXISTS in HAVING is translated while the outer level still collects, so the ORDER BY aggregate gets the name of the HAVING one (A22).

M20_order_expression_over_aggregate_acce._note: Review R5: the refusal of an expression over an aggregate in ORDER BY is gone — the query is accepted and comes back silently unsorted (f7105304) instead of failing loudly.

W1_ask_having_filter_after_slice._note: Review of the spec, W1 (the reviewer's patch verbatim): ASK applies HAVING-as-Filter AFTER the Slice. Passed all 146 tests of the plan: in A21 the matching label was the first solution, so both orders agreed. A23 (and A21 with its "Asset Two" forms) must turn red. Measured: A21 too — its forms now include HAVING (?l = "Asset Two") with LIMIT / OFFSET, where SELECT filters before the slice.

W2_ask_having_via_aggregate_table._note: Review of the spec, W2 (the reviewer's patch verbatim): ASK reuses the HAVING conditions already translated through the aggregate-aware operator table instead of havingAsFilter — the most natural implementation; that table loses the IN list (2f27f300). Passed all 146 tests of the plan: IN was checked in SELECT only (A4), and M8 mutates the shared havingAsFilter, not the ASK path. A24 must turn red. Measured: A21 too — its forms now include HAVING (?l IN ("Asset Two")), which SELECT answers through the full translator.

M23_select_any_order_groups._note: Spec stage (axis coverage, §A159): A12 was green on the base and held by NO mutant — the plan named M9 / M10, the driver shows neither reddens it. Plausible misreading of §18.2.4.1: any ORDER BY groups the SELECT level.

M24_ask_any_order_groups._note: Spec stage (axis coverage, §A159): the ASK half of A12 — any ORDER BY groups the ASK level.
